skill_drafts.name: DataStream Sink Configuration
skill_drafts.description: Configures and deploys a sink function to write DataStream elements to external systems (files, sockets, Kafka) with optional exactly-once delivery semantics via checkpointing.
skill_drafts.objective: Deploy a sink function with appropriate serialization and fault-tolerance guarantees
applicable_signals: DataStream pipeline ready for terminal operation
Target sink system identified and accessible
contraindications: No persistence or external delivery required
Testing with mock outputs or local debugging
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Select sink method', 'detail': 'Choose from writeUsingOutputFormat, writeToSocket, addSink, or FileSink based on target system'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Configure serialization', 'detail': 'Provide SerializationSchema for socket writes or custom object-to-bytes conversion for file outputs'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Enable checkpointing', 'detail': 'Ensure execution environment has checkpointing enabled for exactly-once delivery semantics'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Deploy sink function', 'detail': 'Invoke selected sink method on DataStream; verify elements are being written to target system'}
triggers: Need to persist DataStream to external storage or system
Integrating with Kafka, file systems, or socket endpoints
constraints: Sink function must implement appropriate Flink sink interface
SerializationSchema must be compatible with target system
Checkpointing must be enabled in execution environment for exactly-once semantics
cautions: Custom sink implementations should participate in Flink checkpointing for exactly-once guarantees
FileSink is recommended for reliable file system writes over custom FileOutputFormat implementations
output_contract: Sink function deployed and actively receiving elements from DataStream; checkpoint integration confirmed for exactly-once semantics when required

examples.input: DataStream<String> stream; target system is Apache Kafka
examples.notes: Kafka connector implements sink function with checkpoint participation

examples.input: DataStream<Long> stream; target is file system with exactly-once guarantee
examples.notes: FileSink recommended over writeUsingOutputFormat for reliable file writes

metadata.prompt: Select an appropriate sink method based on target system and delivery requirements. Configure serialization schema if needed. Enable checkpointing for exactly-once semantics when reliability is required. Verify sink function is integrated into the DataStream pipeline.

skill_drafts.name: Iterative Stream Loop Construction
skill_drafts.description: Builds a feedback loop in a DataStream using iterate(), map/filter transformations, and closeWith() to repeatedly process elements until a termination condition is met. Enables stateful iterative computation where elements flow through a transformation body and conditionally re-enter the loop or exit to output.
skill_drafts.objective: Construct and execute a stateful iterative computation on a DataStream
applicable_signals: Termination condition depends on element value or accumulated state
contraindications: No feedback loop or re-entry required
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Create IterativeStream', 'detail': 'Call iterate() on the input DataStream to obtain an IterativeStream handle.'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Define transformation body', 'detail': 'Apply map, filter, or other transformations to the IterativeStream to produce the iteration body.'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Split output and feedback', 'detail': 'Use filter or other operators to partition the transformed stream into feedback (re-entry) and output (exit) branches.'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Close the loop', 'detail': 'Invoke closeWith(feedbackBranch) on the IterativeStream to establish the feedback connection.'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Extract final output', 'detail': 'Obtain the final DataStream from the output branch for downstream sinks or further transformations.'}
triggers: Need to apply repeated transformations until convergence
Implement recursive or feedback-based stream logic
Process elements through multiple passes with state carried between iterations
constraints: Feedback branch must eventually filter out all elements to prevent infinite loops
Output branch and feedback branch must be mutually exclusive or carefully designed to avoid data loss
IterativeStream does not support all DataStream operations; use only map, filter, and similar transformations within the loop body
cautions: Infinite loops occur if the feedback condition never becomes false; always include a termination predicate
Performance may degrade with large iteration counts; monitor for backpressure and resource exhaustion
output_contract: IterativeStream created and configured; loop body defined with transformations; closeWith() invoked to route feedback; final output stream extracted and ready for sinks or further operations.

examples.output: DataStream<Long> containing only integers ≤ 0 after repeated decrement
examples.notes: Subtract 1 from each element in a loop until value ≤ 0; feedback branch filters value > 0, output branch filters value ≤ 0.

metadata.prompt:
1. Call iterate() on the input DataStream to create an IterativeStream.
2. Define the loop body by applying transformations (map, filter, etc.) to the IterativeStream.
3. Split the transformed stream into two parts: one to feed back via closeWith(), one to extract as final output.
4. Invoke closeWith() on the IterativeStream with the feedback branch to establish the loop.
5. Extract the output stream from the non-feedback branch.
Ensure the feedback condition eventually becomes false to prevent infinite loops.

skill_drafts.name: Custom File Output with Object Serialization
skill_drafts.description: Implements custom file output using FileOutputFormat base class with pluggable object-to-bytes conversion logic. Enables writing DataStream elements to files when standard serialization formats are insufficient or non-standard encoding is required.
skill_drafts.objective: Write DataStream elements to files with custom serialization
applicable_signals: DataStream contains objects with non-standard serialization requirements
File output target requires custom encoding
Built-in sink formats do not support the data structure
contraindications: Standard Parquet, Avro, or JSON serialization is adequate
FileSink with built-in formats is sufficient for the use case
Exactly-once delivery semantics required without custom checkpointing support
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Create a class extending FileOutputFormat<T>', 'detail': 'Define the generic type T matching the DataStream element type'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Implement the write(T record) method', 'detail': 'Convert the record object to bytes using custom logic and write to the output stream'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Register the custom format on the DataStream', 'detail': 'Call dataStream.writeUsingOutputFormat(new CustomFileOutputFormat())'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify file output and serialization correctness', 'detail': 'Test with sample data to ensure bytes are written as expected'}
triggers: Standard serialization formats (Parquet, Avro, JSON) insufficient for target data type
Non-standard encoding or binary format required
Custom object-to-bytes conversion logic needed for file persistence
constraints: FileOutputFormat subclass must implement custom write logic
Object-to-bytes conversion must be deterministic and thread-safe
File system must be accessible and writable from all task managers
cautions: Custom serialization logic is responsible for data integrity; test thoroughly with edge cases
For exactly-once delivery guarantees, ensure the custom implementation participates in Flink checkpointing
output_contract: FileOutputFormat subclass implemented with custom write logic; elements serialized and persisted to file system; caller receives confirmation of successful file write or exception on failure

examples.output: File containing serialized CustomObject instances in custom binary format
examples.notes: Custom write() method converts each CustomObject to bytes before file persistence

metadata.prompt: Extend FileOutputFormat and override the write method to implement custom object-to-bytes conversion. Register the custom format via writeUsingOutputFormat() on the DataStream. Ensure the serialization logic handles the target data type and file encoding requirements.
